themes_detail.label: Building Code Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints spiked to 15 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 3.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 329% increase (z-score: 7.67)—suggesting a cluster of code violations or unsafe conditions now emerging in Morris Park/Pelham Parkway.
evidence: 15 Building/Use complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (329% spike)
Z-score of 7.67 indicates extremely rare statistical deviation
312 DOB permits filed in past 90 days (172 alterations, 92 new buildings) suggests active construction/renovation activity may be source
reporting_angles: What buildings are triggering violations? Are they renovation sites, illegal conversions, or commercial-to-residential conversions?
Interview DOB inspectors and residents about what types of violations are driving the spike (structural, safety, zoning, occupancy)

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Explosion Two Weeks Ago
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints peaked at 23 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 2.0 per week—a 1050% spike (z-score: 6.81)—indicating either a coordinated tagging event or a sudden deterioration in city maintenance response in the district.
evidence: 23 graffiti complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1050% spike)
Z-score of 6.81 indicates severe statistical anomaly
No follow-up spike data provided suggests issue may have been addressed or complaints plateaued
reporting_angles: Was there a specific tagging crew or coordinated vandalism event? Interview local business owners and Parks Dept.
How quickly did the city respond to removal? Cross-check with Sanitation Department (DSNY) complaint closure rates

themes_detail.label: Water System Infrastructure Failures
themes_detail.summary: Water System complaints spiked to 66 THREE WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 16.6 per week—a 297% increase (z-score: 4.65)—pointing to a potential water main break, hydrant malfunction, or widespread service disruption affecting residents' access to potable water.
evidence: 66 Water System complaints THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 16.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (297% spike)
Community Board budget requests include 'Other capital budget request for DEP' (repeated request suggests ongoing water infrastructure neglect)
Heat/Hot Water complaints at 1553 over 90 days may indicate correlated boiler/water delivery issues
reporting_angles: What caused the water system spike 3 weeks ago? Interview NYC Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) for incident reports
Are aging pipes in Morris Park/Pelham Parkway driving recurring water complaints? Request infrastructure maintenance records from DEP

themes_detail.label: Electrical System Hazards Two Weeks Ago
themes_detail.summary: ELECTRIC complaints doubled to 20 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 9.2 per week—a 116% increase (z-score: 4.61)—suggesting either a localized power outage, downed lines, or deteriorating electrical infrastructure in multiple buildings.
evidence: 20 ELECTRIC complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 9.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (116% spike)
Overlaps with Water System spike from 3 weeks ago, suggesting possible coordinated infrastructure event or Con Edison service disruption
reporting_angles: Was there a Con Edison outage or service interruption 2 weeks ago? Check utility company incident logs
Are electrical complaints clustering in a specific neighborhood section? Map addresses to identify geographic pattern

themes_detail.label: Rodent and Overgrown Tree Problems
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints reached 12 and tree/branch complaints reached 7 LAST WEEK (160% and 409% spikes respectively, z-scores: 4.1 and 4.62)—signaling convergent environmental deterioration in parks and outdoor spaces, compounded by deferred maintenance.
evidence: Overgrown Tree/Branches: 7 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (409% spike, z-score: 4.62)
Rodent: 12 complaints THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 4.6 weekly average (160% spike, z-score: 4.1)
Community Board has repeated budget requests for 'Reconstruct or upgrade a park or amenity' and 'Clean catch basins,' indicating chronic underfunding of Parks and DEP maintenance
reporting_angles: Are overgrown branches and rodent infestations symptoms of the same parks maintenance backlog? Interview Parks Commissioner and community board about budget cuts
Which specific parks in Morris Park/Pelham Parkway (Pelham Parkway, Van Cortlandt Park borders?) are most affected? Document conditions with photographs
